queries: METR study experienced open-source developers AI tools 19% slower

sources_considered.why: An independent evaluator's measure of the frontier model's autonomous success on software-engineering tasks, dated August 7, 2025.
Only a redirect to the metr.org page.
A secondary table of later re-measurements, not needed.
Measures developer speed, not whether AI can handle coding on its own. Used for the third claim instead.

receipt.public_excerpt: we estimate it has a 50% chance of succeeding at software engineering tasks that would take human professionals (who are unfamiliar with the particular codebase) around 2 hours and 17 minutes.

evidence_items.explanation: The leading frontier model at the post date failed about half the time on software tasks a professional finishes in roughly two hours. That fits the claim that AI could not simply be handed coding work.

receipt.public_excerpt: We find the 80%-time horizon to be around 25m (8m - 65m 95% CI), compared to OpenAI o3’s and Claude Opus 4’s 20m.

evidence_items.explanation: Frontier models reached 80% reliability only on tasks of about 20 to 25 minutes of professional work. That is far from reliably handling software development on their own.

unresolved_gaps: METR's task suite is one benchmark. Its tasks differ from full product development, which tends to be harder, so the measure may overstate AI's ability to handle whole projects.
I found no independent evidence from around the post date of AI reliably building complete, secure software for non-coders. I did not search exhaustively for single anecdotes.
